bank_title: HIP JOINT ULTRASOUND / MUSCULOSKELETAL — PHRASES BANK

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Mild generalized right hip discomfort; rule out joint effusion or tendinopathy.

subs.title: Findings
items: High-frequency sonographic evaluation of the right hip demonstrates normal anterior joint recess with a capsular thickness of 3.2 mm (within normal limits, symmetric with the left side) and no joint effusion.
The iliopsoas tendon and bursa are unremarkable.
The gluteus medius and minimus tendons demonstrate normal uniform fibrillar echotexture without tearing, tendinosis, or insertional calcifications.
The greater trochanteric bursae are collapsed.
The adductor tendon origins and proximal hamstrings are intact.
Dynamic maneuvers show no abnormal snapping.

subs.title: Impression
items: Normal right hip ultrasound. No evidence of joint effusion, hip synovitis, gluteal tendinopathy, or trochanteric bursitis.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute sharp posterior right thigh/buttock pain and "pop" during vigorous water-skiing / sprinting.

subs.title: Findings
items: Overlying the right ischial tuberosity, the conjoined proximal tendons of the hamstrings (semitendinosus, semimembranosus, and biceps femoris) show complete full-thickness disruption and detachment from the ischial tuberosity with a retraction gap measuring 2.4 cm.
A large, heterogeneous, hypoechoic hematoma occupies the ischial space surrounding the retracted tendon stumps.
The sciatic nerve courses immediately adjacent to the hematoma and appears intact without focal entrapment.

subs.title: Impression
items: Complete full-thickness avulsion of the proximal hamstring tendon origin from the right ischial tuberosity with a 2.4 cm retraction gap and large surrounding hematoma.
Urgent orthopedic surgical consultation recommended.

bank.title: 3. Traumatic Rectus Femoris Muscle Tear / Strain (Traumatic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute anterior right thigh pain and localized swelling during a soccer kick.

subs.title: Findings
items: Within the proximal rectus femoris muscle (direct and reflected heads), there is a focal partial-thickness muscle tear involving the musculotendinous junction, measuring 3.5 x 1.8 x 1.2 cm, characterized by feathery disruption of muscle architecture, a central hematoma with fluid clefts, and surrounding intramuscular edema.
The anterior hip joint capsule is normal without effusion.

subs.title: Impression
items: Grade II partial tear of the proximal right rectus femoris muscle musculotendinous junction with an associated intramuscular hematoma.
Normal anterior hip joint capsule without sympathetic effusion.

bank.title: 4. Greater Trochanteric Pain Syndrome — Gluteus Medius Tear & Trochanteric Bursitis (Non-Traumatic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Chronic lateral right hip pain, tenderness over the greater trochanter, and pain when lying on the affected side.

subs.title: Findings
items: Gluteus Medius Tendon: The gluteus medius tendon insertion onto the superolateral facet of the right greater trochanter is thinned, hypoechoic, and demonstrates a focal partial-thickness interstitial tear measuring 8 mm with underlying cortical irregularity and enthesophytes.

Trochanteric Bursae: Marked distension of the subgluteus maximus and subgluteus medius bursae by a well-circumscribed, thick-walled hypoechoic fluid collection measuring 3.2 x 1.4 cm with active hyperemia on power Doppler.
Gluteus Minimus and Iliopsoas: Unremarkable.

subs.title: Impression
items: Moderate-to-severe greater trochanteric pain syndrome, evidenced by a partial-thickness tear of the right gluteus medius tendon and marked trochanteric/subgluteus bursitis with active hyperemia.

bank.title: 5. Infectious / Septic Arthritis or Toxic Synovitis (Non-Traumatic / Pediatric)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: 5-year-old child with acute left hip pain, limp, and low-grade fever.

subs.title: Findings
items: Anterior sonographic evaluation of the left hip joint demonstrates marked distension of the anterior joint capsule with the capsule bowed outward, measuring 8.5 mm in anteroposterior thickness (compared to 3.8 mm on the asymptomatic right side, a difference of 4.7 mm).
The joint space is filled with moderate anechoic to low-level echogenic fluid and mild synovial thickening, with increased power Doppler hyperemia along the capsular reflection.
The femoral head is smoothly marginated without cortical irregularity or subperiosteal abscess.

subs.title: Impression
items: Significant left hip joint effusion (capsular distension = 8.5 mm, asymmetry > 2 mm) with mild synovial hypervascularity.

Findings are non-specific and can be seen in transient toxic synovitis vs. early septic arthritis; urgent clinical correlation, lab workup (WBC, ESR, CRP), and possible joint aspiration are strongly recommended.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Anterior groin pain radiating to the anterior thigh, aggravated by hip flexion.

subs.title: Findings
items: Deep to the iliopsoas muscle and lateral to the femoral vessels, the iliopsoas bursa is markedly distended by a well-defined, thin-walled anechoic cystic collection measuring 4.2 x 1.8 cm, communicating closely with the iliopsoas tendon sheath.
The adjacent iliopsoas tendon is mildly thickened and hypoechoic with mild peritendinous hyperemia.
The hip joint capsule itself is normal without intra-articular effusion.

subs.title: Impression
items: Iliopsoas bursitis (4.2 cm cyst) with associated mild iliopsoas tendinopathy.
Normal anterior hip joint capsule without intra-articular effusion.

bank.title: 7. External Snapping Hip Syndrome (Iliotibial Band Friction) (Non-Traumatic / Dynamic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Audible and painful snapping sensation over the lateral aspect of the hip during walking and hip rotation.

subs.title: Findings
items: Real-time dynamic sonography performed while the patient actively flexes, extends, and rotates the hip demonstrates the thickened posterior border of the iliotibial band (ITB) and anterior border of the gluteus maximus snapping abruptly back and forth in an anterior-posterior direction over the bony prominence of the greater trochanter, reproducing the patient's symptoms.
A small sub-ITB bursa fluid collection is present.

subs.title: Impression
items: Positive dynamic ultrasound findings for external snapping hip syndrome, characterized by abrupt snapping of the iliotibial band over the greater trochanter with localized bursal fluid.
